proposition: According to Melvin-Koushki, Ibn Turka dismissed the Hurufiyya and similar gnostic-messianic movements as perverting the science of letters for non-intellectual and non-Islamic ends, and has sharp words for collapsing occult philosophy into Hurufism or Sufism or dismissing it as mere magic; the pages give no locus for either.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, author of Ibn Turka's works (loci in dissertation ch. 8)
mediation.where: Ibn Turka's works (loci in dissertation ch. 8)
mediation.note: A doctrinal work, not addressed to a judge; the duress rule counts a work as evidence of what he held.
We have the work only as MK summarises or translates it; most of the lettrist works are unedited, so MK's paraphrase cannot be checked against a printed text.
